subject: Intro + demo request — BrightCart AI: checkout optimization use case
messages:
From: Ravi Singh <ravi@brightcart.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightcart.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Quick intro + demo request — BrightCart AI

Hi Sean,

We signed up for a trial on Redwood last week and I wanted to see if we could schedule a short demo next week to understand how Redwood might fit into our checkout personalization pipeline. We’re focusing on latency-sensitive re-rank and personalization models — roughly 600–800 concurrent users during peak, ~12k requests/minute at peak, and we'd like <100ms P95 token latency for short prompts.

A couple quick context points:
- Use case: real-time re-ranking of cart recommendations and one-click upsell copy generation
- Current infra: mixed fleet — some GPU on GCP, some inference in a private cluster
- Timeline: pilot in 6–8 weeks, production in ~3–4 months if pilot looks good

I attached a short requirements doc with traffic numbers and success metrics. Can you and someone from your team run through an evaluation and help us scope a pilot?

Thanks,
Ravi
Ravi Singh
Head of Engineering, BrightCart AI
Attachment: brightcart_requirements_v1.docx (document)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi@brightcart.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 13:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick intro + demo request — BrightCart AI

Hi Ravi — great to meet you (virtually) and thanks for the signup. I’m Sean (Solutions, Redwood Inference). I pulled the doc and skimmed the numbers — this is helpful. A couple quick qualification questions so we can tailor the demo and pilot scope:

1) Are the 12k requests/minute evenly spread across prompts, or do you see spikes concentrated on a few templates?
2) What model family do you expect to serve (open LLMs like Llama-family, smaller specialized models, or do you plan to bring your own fine-tuned checkpoints)?
3) Is the inference workload entirely live traffic, or will you run batch re-ranks as part of the pipeline (we often tune batching differently for batch vs. online)?

Proposed next steps:
- 30m technical walkthrough (demo + Q&A) — my Calendly: https://calendly.com/sean-gallagher/30min — pick any slot that works.
- I’ll include Marissa (SDR) to coordinate logistics and Monica (Customer Success) so we can sketch a pilot MAP during the call.

If you prefer, here are two slots I have next week: Tue 1/20 at 11:00am ET or Wed 1/21 at 3:30pm ET.

Also attaching our standard SLA one-pager so you have it up front.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA_one-pager.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Sean —

Couple quick answers while Ravi is out of meetings:
- Traffic profile: spikes concentrated around promo windows; roughly 70% of traffic hits 3 templates (upsell, cross-sell, discount copy). Outside promos traffic is ~40% lower.
- Model: we are evaluating quantized open models first (strong preference to avoid immediate proprietary model cost), but may bring a 3rd-party fine-tuned model for the checkout copy generator.
- Batch vs live: predominantly live; we do occasional nightly batch scoring for long-tail items.

We’d like to move the call to Wed 1/21 if possible — Tue morning conflicts with leadership sync. If you can do 3:30pm ET on Wed that works for Ravi and me. Also quick question on pricing tiers — do you have guidance on pilot-level pricing or trial credits for inference-intensive pilots?

Alex Turner

Quick answers to your pricing questions:
- For pilots we typically offer time-limited pilot credits plus an evaluation pricing tier that caps per-token spend and includes a reserved slot for Dedicated pools (to preserve latency). We can sketch numbers once we see the model family and token/per-second envelope during the call.
- Marissa will follow up with a short pilot proposal and HubSpot record (RDW-2026-0042) after the demo.
